title: Problem B · personal, and still instant

rows.decision: Build (our rules on top of similarity)
rows.why: This is what makes suggestions sell; a generic tool doesn't know our stores and sizes
rows.giveUp: We tune and test it ourselves. With no data yet, start with a ready tool, then replace it
rows.swapPlan: Ranking sits behind one 'suggest for this person' call: a ready tool answers first, and ours replaces it once there is enough history to test against.
rows.costAt10x: Results are cached per person for a few minutes, so 10× shoppers means about 10× cheap lookups, not 10× heavy computations.

rows.decision: Buy (hosted model for image + text meaning)
rows.why: Solved problem; our edge is how we use it
rows.giveUp: Cost per product, paid once when a product is added
rows.swapPlan: Results are stored with each product, so changing models means processing the catalog once more, in the background.
rows.costAt10x: Cost follows the catalog, not the traffic: 10× shoppers costs nothing extra, and 10× products costs 10× once.

rows.why: Very hard computer vision, not our core business
rows.giveUp: Cost per try-on, so it only opens after a size is chosen
rows.swapPlan: One button and one contract (photo, product and size in; picture out), so another provider plugs into the same button.
rows.costAt10x: Cost grows with try-ons, not visitors; waiting for a chosen size keeps try-ons to shoppers who are close to buying.

rows.why: Standard events, full control of customer data
rows.giveUp: Some upkeep instead of a fully managed service
rows.swapPlan: Events follow one shared contract, so the same stream can feed a managed service instead if the upkeep grows.
rows.costAt10x: Storage grows 10×; raw events are kept 90 days and summaries longer, so the bill grows slower than traffic.

rows.why: Speed is felt on every visit; no tool can make our pages fast for us
rows.giveUp: More frontend work, measured by performance budgets in every release
rows.swapPlan: Nothing to swap: the budgets and techniques are ours, and the hosting underneath can change without touching them.
rows.costAt10x: Prepared first pages and page-by-page loading keep each visit's cost flat, so 10× visitors is mostly 10× cache hits.

rows.decision: Buy (image service with the right size per phone)
rows.giveUp: A monthly bill, kept small by preparing common sizes in advance
rows.swapPlan: Every image address goes through one helper, so moving to another service is one change plus a cache warm-up.
rows.costAt10x: Common sizes are prepared once and cached, so 10× visitors mostly means cache hits, not new work.
